components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; height: 32px; padding: 0 10px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 10px; background: var(--primary, #db2777); color: var(--primary-foreground, #ffffff); font: 500 14px 'Geist Variable', sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: all 150ms; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--primary, #db2777) 80%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--ring, #ec4899); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in srgb, var(--ring, #ec4899) 50%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.css: .ds-glossary { font: 12px/20px 'Geist Variable', sans-serif; color: var(--foreground, #302b3b); } .ds-glossary summary { display: flex; width: fit-content; align-items: flex-start; gap: 4px; list-style: none; cursor: pointer; border-radius: 4px; color: var(--muted-foreground, #75636c); user-select: none; } .ds-glossary summary::-webkit-details-marker { display: none; } .ds-glossary summary svg { margin-top: 3px; flex-shrink: 0; transition: transform 0.15s; } .ds-glossary[open] summary svg { transform: rotate(90deg); } .ds-glossary summary:hover { color: var(--foreground, #302b3b); } .ds-glossary summary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in srgb, #ec4899 50%, transparent); } .ds-glossary dl { margin: 10px 0 0; display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(15rem, 100%), 1fr)); gap: 8px 24px; } .ds-glossary dt { font-weight: 500; } .ds-glossary dd { margin: 2px 0 0; color: var(--muted-foreground, #75636c); } .ds-gl-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; height: 20px; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 26px; background: #fbf0f3; color: #975263; font-weight: 500; } .ds-gl-proc { background: #edf3fa; color: #3d6b97; }

narrative.overview:
Simplink is a drafting desk for mapping product knowledge. The desk is quiet: violet-tinted paper (`lavender-paper`), white card surfaces, plum ink, and hairline lilac borders. The map is where colour lives. Four muted node-type hues (rose, blue, sage, ochre) mark goals, procedures, capabilities and states across graph nodes, badges and type dots. One brand accent, **Simp Pink**, marks what the author is touching right now: the active view, the selected node, the primary action, a link.

Controls should feel **soft and approachable**: gently rounded, tinted rather than outlined in grey, and calm at the density needed for long editing sessions next to an editor and a terminal. Structure comes from tonal layers and hairlines, not shadows. Problems are the exception: error red and warning ochre may interrupt anywhere, because "problems first" is a product principle.

The system rejects four looks: generic grey shadcn (no tint, no type colour), neon dev-tool dark, marketing gloss (gradients, glass, hero type inside the app), and rainbow chrome (node-type colours leaking into navigation, buttons or page frame).
keyCharacteristics: Violet-tinted neutrals everywhere. No pure greys in the light theme's foreground, border or background roles.
One brand accent (Simp Pink) for selection, the active state and primary action.
Four node-type colours, each with a wash, used only for knowledge-graph semantics.
Flat at rest. Lift only appears on overlays, drawers and selection.
Geist Variable throughout. Cascadia Code for source and IDs.
Full light and dark themes; light is the default.

rules.name: The Readable Ink Rule
rules.body: Type-coloured text uses `--type-ink`, never `--type-color`. The lighter type colours are for edges, dots and minimap fills, where 3:1 is enough.

rules.name: The One Pen Rule
rules.body: Simp Pink means "this is active, selected or the next action." Never use it for decoration, section fills or illustration.

rules.name: The Map Ink Rule
rules.body: Node-type colours belong to knowledge-graph semantics only: badges, node left-edges, type dots and graph filters. They never colour navigation, buttons or page chrome.

rules.name: The Tinted Paper Rule
rules.body: Neutrals carry a violet cast. A new surface or text colour that reads as neutral grey is a bug.

rules.name: The Weight Not Face Rule
rules.body: Build hierarchy with Geist weights between 550 and 700 and with tracking. Never add a second sans or a serif to the workspace.

rules.name: The Two Scales Rule
rules.body: App chrome stays compact (9–25px). Reading scale (14–32px, generous margins) applies only inside `.markdown` previews.

rules.name: The Lift On State Rule
rules.body: A surface at rest has no shadow beyond a node settle. Shadows mean floating (overlay, drawer, popover) or selected.

dos: **Do** reach for theme tokens (`bg-card`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-border`, `--type-color`) instead of literal colours, and define every new colour for both light and dark.
**Do** keep Simp Pink for the active, selected or primary action, at most one primary button per view.
**Do** carry node type through the `--type-color` / `--type-bg` class mechanism so badges, nodes and dots stay in sync.
**Do** separate surfaces with lilac hairlines and tonal steps, and keep controls at 32px with a 10px radius.
**Do** keep errors and warnings visible in chrome (count bubbles, banners) using Alarm Red and Amber Ochre washes.
**Do** give every enum or code a visible explanation through a Glossary disclosure; a `title` tooltip may only repeat what is already visible.
**Do** map third-party widget themes (React Flow) onto the tokens in both themes instead of accepting their stock greys.
**Do** respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. The global reset already disables animation and transitions.
donts: **Don't** fall back to generic grey shadcn: untinted neutrals, stock `neutral` greys, or missing type colours.
**Don't** drift into neon dev-tool dark. Dark mode is plum (#17131d), not black, and has no glowing accents.
**Don't** add marketing gloss inside the app: gradients, glassmorphism, oversized hero type or decorative illustration.
**Don't** let node-type colours leak into navigation, buttons or page chrome (rainbow chrome).
**Don't** add resting shadows to cards or panels. Lift is reserved for overlays, drawers and selection.
**Don't** use a solid red fill for destructive buttons. Use the 10% red wash with red text.
**Don't** set text in `--type-color` or a raw status colour on its wash. Use the ink (The Readable Ink Rule).
